A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KromHC work and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendices J and K.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original LLM-pretraining and downstream results, residual-width experiments, gradient analyses, and an ablation of shared scaling factors.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds system-efficiency measurements in Appendix J and a factorization-choice ablation in Appendix K.

M1.justification: KromHC's Kronecker-product construction, permutation-mixture factors, pre/post mappings, and Equation (14) remain unchanged. Appendix K tests factorizations already allowed by Remark 4.5, rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use FineWeb-Edu pretraining and the same downstream benchmarks and CORE task suite. The added efficiency and factorization studies introduce no new dataset, domain, or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator identities remain standard residual connections, mHC, and mHC-lite. Table 9 reuses existing comparators. The written correction to Equation (4) does not establish a changed evaluated implementation, and Appendix E's suggested HC alternative is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Appendix J introduces throughput, step-time, and GPU-memory measurements using pure PyTorch, 12 blocks, four streams, and eight RTX 6000 GPUs. Appendix K compares two factorization configurations at eight streams. Existing training settings remain stable; Section 5.4's correction from 12 to 16 streams matches v1's existing figure and table.

E4.justification: New Appendix K tests whether stronger factorization restrictions hurt performance by comparing 4×2 with 2×2×2 at eight streams and 12 blocks. The existing scaling-factor ablation, residual-width analysis, and gradient analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Figure 5's EMA-variance shading. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new appendix results also lack uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Corrections include Table 4's 12-block mHC average, 44.5 to 47.5, and six-block mHC-lite WG score, 53.4 to 52.4; Table 5's six-block KromHC average, 19.5 to 17.3; and Table 6's four-stream parameter overhead, 0.24 to 0.96M. New Table 9 reports KromHC throughput +19.23%, step time -16.24%, and memory -1.15% versus pure-PyTorch mHC. Appendix K reports train loss/BPB lower by 0.002/0.003 for 2×2×2 versus 4×2.

T1.justification: Equation (4) revises the written mHC residual mapping from SK(alpha·mat(x'W)+b) to SK(alpha·mat(x'W+b)), moving the bias inside both reshaping and scalar multiplication. The Kronecker-closure theorem and Appendix B proof remain unchanged; the added proof citation supplies attribution rather than new theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: exact double stochasticity through Kronecker factors, O(n^2 C) parameter scaling, and competitive LLM performance with fewer parameters and no custom kernels. Wording edits and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds an expressivity critique of original HC and recommends mHC-style parameterization without Sinkhorn-Knopp. Appendix J qualifies efficiency comparisons because the pure-PyTorch mHC baseline may underrepresent specialized-kernel performance. Appendix K interprets its ablation as evidence that restrictive factorizations need not sacrifice performance.

D1.justification: Appendix J newly documents the pure-PyTorch implementations and hardware/model setup for system measurements. Existing initialization, optimizer and hyperparameter values, and code access are retained. Table 7 relabels the residual-connection learning rate without changing its value.

R1.justification: v2 adds Taranenko (2023) as a source for Kronecker closure and replaces the COPA citation to Roemmele et al. (2011) with Gordon et al. (2012). Appendix E further distinguishes original HC from mHC. Most other reference edits update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording, capitalization, and notation-consistency edits, updates publication and correspondence information, expands Appendix E, and adds two short appendix sections. The main narrative and section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 9, changes result-table highlighting and some captions/labels, and reflows references and appendix material. Figure 8 is relocated and reduced in size; the existing diagrams and plotted analyses are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects consequential reporting inconsistencies in Tables 4–6 and adds targeted evidence about practical efficiency and factorization choice. The explicit pure-PyTorch caveat improves interpretation of the speed comparison. These are limited gains: the new ablation lacks uncertainty estimates, and Table 4's six-block mHC-lite average remains inconsistent with its displayed task scores.
